stimuli.description: personal lighting system consisted of two Hue Aurelle Rectangular Lights (Signify) that measure 120 by 30 cm, of which one was mounted on the ceiling, and another was placed on the desk. The participants faced the desk light and used a laptop screen to mimic office activities. The illuminance of the laptop screen was fixed at a low level. When participants had personal control over CCT, they controlled the ceiling and the desk light simultaneously. CCT range between 2700 K and 5700 K in 20 perceptually equal steps. Illuminance was fixed at 498.9 ± 5.2 lux at the eye, air temperature at 17.2 °C±0.3 °C, the mean radiant temperature at 17.2 °C±0.2 °C, the relative humidity at 40-48%, and the air speed at 0.15-0.26 m/s.
stimuli.source: Fig. S1 and 2.2.2 Personal lighting system

tables.description: Parameter estimates for the effect of having and exercising control as well as the effect of actual CCT on all outcome measures.

limitations: The current study investigated only the causal route from visual comfort (induced by self-selected light condition) to thermal comfort. Similarly, one could in future work study the opposite direction.

The reference conditions in this study were not rated with a low visual comfort. In real-life situations where visual comfort is considerably compromised by CCT, the benefits of personal control of CCT may be more pronounced.
Participants were only allowed to control the CCT at the beginning of Period 2, potentially underestimating the positive effects of personal control of CCT.
The study was not able to distinguish the effects of merely perceiving control from the effects of personalization (i.e., exercising control) based on the regression models.

The test duration in this study was 70 min. The beneficial effects of personal control may accrue over a time span of days. Therefore, it is recommended to investigate the effects of personal control over CCT in the long term.
The sample size was too small to detect the effects.
